name: Talon Systems Grav-Pulse Emitter GPE-3 'Downdraft'
description:
A directed gravitational weapon that projects a focused pulse of gravitational force in a cone-shaped area of effect. Unlike the localized gravity wells of the GL-3 Crush Depth, the Downdraft produces a broad directional push — effectively a gravitational shockwave that slams everything in its path to the ground with 8-12G of downward force for approximately 0.5 seconds.

Talon Systems developed the GPE-3 as a non-lethal crowd control weapon that exploits gravitational manipulation at lower intensities than Arcturus's lethal GL-3. The Downdraft's pulse is calibrated to incapacitate rather than kill — the brief duration prevents the sustained compression that causes organ failure, while the force magnitude is sufficient to drop even augmented targets to the ground and prevent them from rising for several seconds.

The weapon's cone-shaped area of effect covers a 15-meter wide swath at maximum range, making it effective against groups of targets. The gravitational pulse passes through cover and concealment — walls, furniture, and vehicles provide no protection against a force that acts on mass itself.
legality: Non-lethal classification at standard settings — military restricted at elevated power
specifications:
caliber: N/A — directional gravitational pulse
effective_range: 10-80 meters, 15-meter cone width at max range
rate_of_fire: 1 pulse per 8 seconds
capacity: 10 pulses per power cell
weight: 14 kg
power_source: Gravitational manipulation power cell
tactical_use: The Downdraft is deployed for crowd dispersal, area denial, and non-lethal incapacitation of groups. The weapon's cone-shaped effect allows a single operator to knock an entire group prone in a single pulse, creating a window for restraint, extraction, or withdrawal. The gravitational pulse's ability to pass through cover makes it effective against barricaded subjects — the operator does not need line of sight to the target, only line of effect to the space they occupy.
cultural_context: The GPE-3 has sparked intense debate about the use of gravitational manipulation as a non-lethal tool. At standard settings, the weapon is rarely lethal — but 'rarely' is not 'never.' Individuals with osteoporosis, spinal injuries, or pregnancy are at significantly elevated risk from the sudden gravitational load. Rights organizations have called for the weapon's reclassification after several deaths in crowd-control scenarios involving vulnerable populations.
story_hooks: A Downdraft was used against a protest crowd that included a pregnant woman. The gravitational pulse caused injuries that resulted in a miscarriage. The operator followed standard engagement protocol. The legal and ethical aftermath threatens to end gravitational weapon deployment in civilian-adjacent scenarios.

Someone has modified a GPE-3 to project its pulse upward rather than downward — the modified weapon launches targets into the air with 10G of upward force, and gravity handles the lethal landing. The modification is crude but effective.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Graviton Lens GL-3 'Crush Depth'

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, anvil-shaped emitter cannon with a pronounced barrel assembly that flares outward like an inverted trumpet. The weapon's silhouette suggests raw, uncompromising force — all sharp angles and purposeful mass. At first glance, it reads as heavy ordnance masquerading as crowd control, industrial and imposing rather than sleek.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 94 cm | Width (at emitter flare): 32 cm | Height: 28 cm | Barrel extension: 38 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and grounded — 14 kg of dense engineering that demands respect. The weight is front-loaded toward the flared emitter, creating a deliberate downward bias that mirrors the weapon's gravitational function. Requires a firm two-handed grip; single-handed operation is possible but exhausting over repeated use.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced titanium-composite frame with aluminum heat-dispersal fins. The emitter cone is constructed from aerospace-grade carbon-ceramic to withstand repeated gravitational pulse discharge without warping.
physical_description.finish: Matte gun-metal gray with brushed titanium accents. The emitter cone features a subtle iridescent sheen — a telltale sign of the gravitational field calibration layer. Surface is deliberately non-reflective to prevent targeting laser detection.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal gray | Accents: brushed titanium silver | Emitter interior: deep charcoal with faint cyan energy tracery
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with embedded cooling channels running lengthwise. The texture is aggressive — fine diagonal crosshatching — designed to prevent slip even with wet or gloved hands. Warm to the touch after extended use due to passive heat dissipation.
distinctive_features: Flared emitter cone with radiating acceleration rings visible on interior surface
Integrated thermal management vents along the barrel shaft — five horizontal slits per side
Cyan-blue power cell indicator ring that circles the grip junction, pulsing with charge state
Recessed targeting reticle plate above the grip — no traditional sight, only calibration markings
Gravitational field harmonics display strip along the left side — three digital readouts showing pulse frequency, cone angle, and force magnitude
Heavy-duty Picatinny rail on dorsal surface for mounting stabilization equipment
Discharge chamber vents with faint residual electromagnetic shimmer after firing
Rubber-capped cable port on rear for field power coupling
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TALON SYSTEMS stamped in bold sans-serif font on the upper receiver. Model designation 'GPE-3' etched into the left side of the barrel. Serialization plate mounted flush on the grip with GLMZ compliance certificates and power safety ratings. Faint Φ currency stamp indicating military-contractor tier pricing.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show battle-worn finish with scuffed matte coating, micro-fractures in the emitter cone ceramic from repeated gravitational stress, and carbonized heat streaking around the discharge vents. Well-maintained examples retain the brushed titanium shine; heavy use specimens develop a dull, almost charred appearance from thermal cycling.
